clue.text: A way to interrupt European supporter

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so the way goes into the middle of the European

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A fan of Europe gets cut off mid-sentence by someone on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a devoted advocate or follower of a cause, a committed backer.

clue.text: Or twice cut Plaid Cymru off — see red?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or not right, so the letters are jumbled
twice says the word before it is written two times over

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold, a tincture

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter of Plaid is lopped off

parts.note: taken as written, less its tail
taken as written; Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party

explanation.surface: Plaid Cymru, the Welsh nationalist party, is snubbed and someone gets furious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles OR; 'cut' trims PLAID to PLAI; 'off' shuffles ORORPLAICYMRU. 'see' is a link: red is an example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is one of the three basic hues from which painters mix all others, an example of the class.

clue.text: Party without independence, English attack

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the party wraps round the letter

parts.note: SNP is the Scottish National Party
I is a short form for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A Scottish party stripped of its independence cause launches an assault on the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means 'outside'; the SNP campaigns for Scottish independence, which sharpens the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to make sly critical attacks, as a hidden marksman shoots from cover.

clue.text: Labour and Conservative mostly promise medical protection?

parts.note: LAB is the short form for the Labour Party

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: an oath is a solemn promise

explanation.surface: Both main parties pledge to safeguard the health service.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the 'protection' is a garment, not policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A white garment worn by doctors and scientists shields their clothes, a playful sense of protection.

clue.text: Early entertainment in conflict — politicians turn inside

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: inside says the turn sits within the politicians

parts.note: MPs are Members of Parliament
U as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: During a war, politicians perform a U-turn at the start of proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening acts that get an audience going before the main show come first in the evening.

clue.text: Honours patients collectively as nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, so the two letters cradle the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
a ward is a hospital room full of patients

explanation.surface: Medals go to all the patients because they act as nurses.
explanation.definitionFit: Prizes and decorations conferred in recognition are honours bestowed.

clue.text: Worn-out porno mag with hard paper

indicators.note: worn-out means battered and broken, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tatty adult magazine printed on stiff paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly treatise on a single subject is a paper in the academic sense.

clue.text: Little money for investment, an atonement?

indicators.note: investment is putting in, so the word an is put into the money

parts.note: pence are small coins
taken as written

explanation.surface: Putting a few coppers into savings as a way of making amends.
explanation.definitionFit: An act done to make up for wrongdoing is a form of atonement.

clue.text: Sweet talk of circuit training

indicators.note: training as in shaping or drilling into new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gym chatter about circuit training described as pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective praising the talk; it is the noun, a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of mixed chopped fruit in syrup, served as a pudding course.

clue.text: Small leading politician, only half visible

indicators.note: only half visible means just the first half of the word shows

parts.note: a government minister is a leading politician

explanation.surface: A short senior politician can barely be seen over the lectern.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective or prefix it means tiny or diminutive, like a miniature.

clue.text: See 27
Cope with gain (Con)

parts.note: to make money is to gain it
to do someone is to cheat or con them

explanation.surface: A Conservative copes by winning more seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a Conservative label in brackets; it is the verb 'swindle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to manage with whatever is available, getting by.

clue.text: Running country? Hunt's hospital department poor?

parts.note: the party that is in is the one in power, running the country
to dig is to hunt or search
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Jeremy Hunt, the health secretary, may run hospital departments poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt was the UK Health Secretary, which makes 'Hunt' look like a name; it is a verb meaning search.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy and destitute, lacking money.

clue.text: Liberal phony and jerks — they could easily go under

indicators.note: liberal means free or loose, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
tics are involuntary jerks

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is a fake, and the jerks backing him could sink without trace.
explanation.definitionFit: People readily put into a trance are easily sent under, as a subject goes under hypnosis.

clue.text: Idiots: they dig rows, say

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union, people who dig

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat

explanation.surface: Fools: miners who pick quarrels, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests quarrels (rhyming with cows); it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit or dunce is a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Leader missing, right: no, brief appearance?

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so these letters drop out

parts.note: David Cameron was the Conservative leader and Prime Minister
N stands for no, as on a yes/no form

explanation.surface: With the party leader gone and the right wing absent, a short appearance looks unlikely.
explanation.definitionFit: A small walk-on part played by a well-known performer is a fleeting appearance.

clue.text: Tail-end wicket

definitions.meaning: the remaining end of something cut down, such as a tree or a limb
one of the three upright sticks forming the wicket in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary snippet: the lower-order batsman loses his wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumping also means campaigning, fitting the election theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub left after cutting is the end portion, and in cricket the upright sticks make up the wicket.

clue.text: Stop working — mostly rubbish on strike

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: tripe is nonsense, rubbish
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: Walking out of work: mostly nonsense, says someone on the picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: When a circuit breaker trips, the supply cuts off and equipment ceases to function.

clue.text: Place that could support life peer — chose differently

indicators.note: differently means in another way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A life peer in the Lords might have voted another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life' looks like part of 'life peer', a member of the House of Lords; it belongs in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A region where living organisms can exist, a self-sustaining biological system.

clue.text: Triumph to follow

definitions.meaning: to come after, as an heir takes over

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to achieve success and to come next in a line, as a new leader does.

clue.text: They move in pants, when topless

indicators.note: topless means without the top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: in US English pants are trousers

explanation.surface: Something wriggles in someone's underwear when they strip to the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants are underwear; the American sense, trousers, is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who rouse others stir and excite them, so they move people.

clue.text: Party and union check online stream

parts.note: a do is a party
CH is the chess abbreviation for check
E as in e-mail, electronic or online

explanation.surface: Party and trade union officials vet an internet video stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet of water directed at the body for cleansing is a stream, the original sense.

clue.text: Chooses UKIP? Cost, horrendous

indicators.note: horrendous means dreadful or a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; UKIP is the UK Independence Party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A voter backs UKIP, the anti-EU party, whatever the dreadful price.
explanation.definitionFit: To select from among many is to choose.

clue.text: See 2
One with serious conviction in centre, filling up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, so backwards
in signals that the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A committed believer is in the middle, stuffing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' suggests belief, but means a criminal sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner serving a whole-of-life term has the gravest of criminal sentences.

clue.text: See 27
Rebel Nigel Farage — iconic TV broadcast for talks about working conditions

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; Nigel Farage was UKIP's leader
taken as written

explanation.surface: Maverick Nigel Farage appears on a memorable TV programme for a debate on workers' rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Negotiations between unions and employers over pay and terms are talks on employment conditions.

clue.text: Loads of cuts (time for Left)?

indicators.note: time for Left means the letter for time replaces the letter for left

parts.note: slashes are cuts, including spending cuts

explanation.surface: Plenty of spending cuts: is it time for the Left to take over?
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden stores or hoards of something are plentiful supplies, large amounts.

clue.text: Speech in place

definitions.meaning: a formal talk given to an audience
where someone lives or can be found

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal oration and the location of a house, as written on an envelope.
